I farm a small 4.5 mu wheat-maize rotation plot with well irrigation, and I have a long time horizon in mind because I have been doing this for 40 years. On this kind of land, I do not chase extreme input levels. I manage for stable yield, controlled cost, and low labor risk, especially since my household is small and some labor is off-farm. Because I am educated and experienced, I rely on improved seed and disciplined field management rather than excessive fertilizer or sprays. For winter wheat, I will keep fertilizer moderate and use irrigation at the key stages because wheat in Hebei responds well to timely water and nitrogen, but too much input is wasteful on a small plot. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me stronger and more reliable yield potential in this system. I will keep tillage practical, mainly rotary tillage, because it fits my scale and saves labor while still preparing a workable seedbed after the previous crop. I will use pesticides only as needed for routine weed and pest control, not aggressively. Overall, I will aim for steady, efficient production from both crops with inputs matched to my irrigated conditions and my small household labor supply.
